FINDING_ID: IM_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.96  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.86  
DESCRIPTION: In [dynamic_management.py:5045](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5045), `process_round()` only runs Area 6 failure detection for models present in `responses`. A dispatched model that vanishes entirely never reaches `detect_failure()` or `get_recovery()`, so it gets no recovery action, stays in the active set, and can even let a missing PM evade the intended abort path. The immune layer later treats the same absence as a failure in [dynamic_management.py:5153](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5153), so Area 6 and Area 7 diverge on the same event.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Iterate over the expected dispatched or active model set, not just `responses.items()`. For absent models, synthesize a missing-response failure and feed it through `FailureHandler` so recovery, active-model updates, PM abort logic, and immune telemetry all share one failure truth.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.91  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.82  
DESCRIPTION: The false-positive self-correction is a no-op. `self_diagnose()` mutates `_sensitivity_decay` in [dynamic_management.py:3945](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3945), but detector sensitivity is computed by `effective_window()` in [dynamic_management.py:2615](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2615), which never reads `_sensitivity_decay` at all. The system logs “Self-adjusted” while detector behaviour remains unchanged.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either wire `_sensitivity_decay` into the actual trigger math in `effective_window()` or remove that knob and adjust a parameter that the detector really uses, such as the effective window or pathology thresholds.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.89  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.79  
DESCRIPTION: Deferred-remediation approval is backdated to the original diagnosis round. In [dynamic_management.py:5949](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5949), `approve_deferred_remediation()` reuses `deferred["round"]` for `_record_adjustment()` and `set_remediation_state()`. If a human approves the fix several rounds later, outcome verification starts counting from the old round, so the system can judge the remediation before any post-approval evidence exists.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Pass the actual approval round into `approve_deferred_remediation()` and use that for `applied_round` and adjustment logging. Keep the original diagnosis round as metadata only.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.87  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.77  
DESCRIPTION: The `mu+novelty` “remediation” is only a log entry. In [dynamic_management.py:5728](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5728), `apply_diagnosis()` records an adjustment to `stop_signal_priority`, but there is no corresponding config field or control path in the real stop logic at [dynamic_management.py:2271](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2271). The code claims it now prefers novelty over `mu`, but stopping behaviour does not actually change.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add a real control flag that `DiminishingReturnsDetector.stop()` or `process_round()` reads when `mu` is diagnosed as unreliable, or treat this diagnosis as advisory only and stop recording it as an applied adaptation.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.83  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.72  
DESCRIPTION: Deferred remediations can be queued repeatedly with no deduplication or damping. The DEFER path in [dynamic_management.py:5815](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5815) appends a new pending item and returns without recording an immune adjustment or any “already pending” state. Because damping only checks `_immune_adjustments` in [dynamic_management.py:5700](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5700), the same recurring diagnosis can enqueue the same deferred fix every round.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Key deferred items by remediation identity, refuse to enqueue a second `PENDING` copy, and count a pending deferred remediation as active for damping purposes until it is approved or rejected.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F006  
SEVERITY: 0.78  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.64  
DESCRIPTION: Persistent `mu` pathology never updates its adaptive state. The `mu` diagnosis path at [dynamic_management.py:2665](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2665) emits a diagnosis but does not increment `_pathology_counts["mu"]`, while the recovery branch at [dynamic_management.py:2703](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2703) assumes that count exists. As a result, repeated `mu` distortions never escalate, `effective_window("mu", ...)` never learns from persistence, and natural-resolution bookkeeping for `mu` never triggers.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Mirror the `kappa` path: increment the `mu` pathology count when diagnosed, include the occurrence in evidence, and only reset and mark resolution when the condition actually clears.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

**Validation**
Exp15 finding 4.5 looks genuinely fixed in the immune path: `recovery_actions` is carried through `RoundResult` in [dynamic_management.py:4800](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L4800), populated in [dynamic_management.py:5042](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5042), and written into the result in [dynamic_management.py:5320](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5320).

Exp15 finding 4.6 also looks fixed: per-model yield is now fed from `new_findings_flat`, not raw round findings, in [dynamic_management.py:5089](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5089) and [dynamic_management.py:5126](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5126). I do not see an immune-scope basis to reopen that no-fix-needed call. Exp15 finding 4.3 is outside the stated immune boundary.
